relationships.subject: TRPV1 nociceptors
relationships.evidence_quote: After two weeks, TRPV1 activated mice had skin patches with anagen HFs while no hair growth was detected in controls (Figure 2A).

relationships.subject: CGRP
relationships.evidence_quote: Intradermal CGRP injection was able to phenocopy the increased Annexin V signal and reduced dermal macrophage frequency induced by TRPV1 activation (Figure 4D).

relationships.subject: TRPV1 nociceptors
relationships.evidence_quote: the CGRP antagonist, CGRP8–37, significantly reduced both CD9+CD26+ fibroblast induction and hair growth, (Figure 2H, I and J), highlighting CGRP's involvement in TRPV1-induced fibroblast and hair growth phenotypes.

relationships.subject: Spp1
relationships.evidence_quote: Treating TRPV1 activated mice with Spp1 blocking antibody significantly attenuated hair growth (Figure 2F), demonstrating a role for Spp1 in this context.

relationships.subject: Axl signaling
relationships.evidence_quote: R428 administration reduced the efficiency of CD9+CD26+ fibroblasts induction after TRPV1 activation (Figure 5F).

key_findings: Chemogenetic activation of dermal TRPV1 nociceptors triggers CGRP-dependent dermal macrophage apoptosis, Spp1+ fibroblast induction and hair growth.
Epidermal abrasion induces Spp1+ fibroblasts in a TRPV1 neuron-dependent manner.
